comparison.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an angular gripper stop; PR-2015 turns a suspended humanoid upper body half a revolution and brings it gently to rest.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses precise two-tool countertorque and later cycles a mechanism; PR-2015 regulates the momentum of a freely yawing 18.3 kg suspended assembly through push and catch actions.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° opening with low drift over three cycles; PR-2015 requires approximately 180° net rotation, under 1°/s for one second, without blows or collisions.
comparison.reason: Both concern robot hardware, but suspended-load momentum control is a different tested ability from threaded stop adjustment; all material rubric details are present.
